question: According to the ILAE 2017 Classification of Seizure Types, which feature BEST distinguishes a focal-onset seizure from a generalised-onset seizure?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Tonic-clonic movements can occur in both focal-onset (with bilateral propagation) and primary generalised-onset seizures; they do not distinguish the two.

answers.text: Origin within networks limited to one cerebral hemisphere

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. A focal-onset seizure originates within networks of one hemisphere (which may or may not spread bilaterally), whereas a generalised-onset seizure engages bilateral networks from the start.
Duration ≥5 minutes defines status epilepticus, not the focal-vs-generalised distinction.
Awareness (consciousness) is a secondary descriptor within focal seizures (focal aware vs focal impaired awareness), not the primary criterion separating focal from generalised onset.

overallFeedback.feedback: Review the ILAE 2017 framework: onset localisation (focal vs generalised vs unknown) is determined by the hemisphere(s) engaged at seizure initiation, not by motor semiology or duration.
Well done. Focal onset = one-hemisphere networks; generalised onset = bilateral networks from the outset.
